tagline: Holiday street names, and dunes made from a volcano.
intro: From Oregon 31 at County Road 5-10, the Christmas Valley byway reaches into high desert country. In Christmas Valley, a developer laid out streets named Candy Lane and Mistletoe Road, promoting an agricultural community in land a tax-court judge later described as arid and isolated.
East of town, the sand dunes rise as high as sixty feet. Much of that shifting ground is ash and pumice from Mount Mazama, carried here by the wind after the eruption that formed Crater Lake.

moments.title: Christmas Valley
moments.text: Holiday street names recall a planned community promoted to would-be farmers, though few of the buyers ever moved there.

moments.title: Christmas Valley Sand Dunes
moments.text: Ash and pumice from Mount Mazama make dunes up to sixty feet high in the desert east of town.

practical: Vehicle use in the dunes is confined to designated areas and routes; campsites in the protected area are primitive, without water or restrooms.

sources.label: Bureau of Land Management, Christmas Valley Back Country Byway
